objectives.title: Employment
objectives.text: Bring more working age residents into sustained work. The gap is inactivity, mostly ill health, not unemployment.

objectives.title: Pay
objectives.text: Raise the pay of jobs located in Burnley towards England's. Workplace pay has stayed at about 80% of England's for ten years.

objectives.title: Resilience
objectives.text: Widen and steady the business base. Firms in Burnley survive badly, retail output is falling, and one sector carries a large share of output.

rows.title: Long term sickness
rows.target: Reduce the excess of residents inactive through long term sickness or disability by a quarter to a half by the 2031 Census, and hold the gain to 2036.
rows.baseline: 5,046 residents, 6.7% of those aged 16 and over (Census 2021)
rows.arithmetic: At England's 4.1% Burnley would have about 3,083 of its 75,205 residents aged 16 and over in this group, so the excess is about 1,960. A quarter to a half is about 490 to 980.
rows.indicator: Census 2031; in between, the Universal Credit health caseload and PIP cases as exposure counts

rows.title: Employment
rows.target: Close a third to a half of the inactivity gap to England by 2036.
rows.arithmetic: A third to a half of about 3,720 residents is about 1,240 to 1,860.
rows.indicator: Pooled survey years; payroll each month as the check

rows.title: Workplace pay
rows.target: Raise Burnley's workplace median full time pay from 80.4% of England's to between 82% and 85% by 2036.
rows.arithmetic: 82% of £817.0 is £669.9; 85% is £694.5. That closes about 8% to 24% of the £160.2 gap.

rows.title: Jobs
rows.target: Raise jobs density from 0.72 to between 0.75 and 0.78 by 2036.
rows.arithmetic: 0.03 to 0.06 more jobs per resident, about 1,830 to 3,660 jobs on today's residents.
rows.indicator: Jobs density in the ONS labour market tables each October

rows.title: Business resilience
rows.target: Raise five year survival from 27.5% (2019 cohort) to between 33% and 38% for the 2031 birth cohort, and hold wholesale and retail output at or above its 2024 level of £523m.
rows.indicator: ONS business demography each November; regional GVA each autumn
